text: Read aloud to them while they're in the bath. Their pick of book, your best voice for every character.
Brush their hair for ten slow minutes. No talking unless they start it.
Paint each other's nails. You each pick the other's color, and nobody gets a veto.
Fall asleep on a video call together. Whoever wakes first hangs up quietly and texts goodnight.
Feed each other breakfast in bed. Hands only, no forks, crumbs are part of the deal.
Fall asleep holding hands. Whoever lets go first makes the coffee.
Wash their hair at the sink like a fancy salon: warm water, slow scalp massage, towel turban to finish.
Teach each other a skill you're secretly proud of: a card trick, a recipe, a song. Twenty minutes each.
Give them a hand massage while they tell you about their day, start to finish, no interruptions.
Make a playlist where every song is tied to one specific night together. Play it start to finish, lights low.
Everyone drops their phone in a bowl by the door for the whole evening. First to reach for theirs does the dishes.
Run their morning for them: coffee made, clothes laid out, towel warmed, sent off with a kiss.
Bathe them and wash their hair. No phones in the room, no rushing, and they don't lift a finger.
Give them a full-body massage with no expectation of anything after. And mean it.
Lie face to face and find every scar, freckle, and mark on their skin. Ask for the story behind each one.
Spend a whole morning in bed: no alarms, no screens, just talking, dozing, and whatever else wanders in.
Start a Sunday-night ritual in bed: one thing you loved about them this week, one thing you need, one thing you want to try.
Do their skincare for them, slowly and carefully, like it's the most important job you'll have all week.
Rub lotion into every inch of them after their shower. Every inch they offer, anyway.
Sleep naked tonight, skin to skin, with nothing expected. Just notice everything.
Every night this week, end the day with a wordless kiss that lasts a full minute. On the last night, don't stop at a minute.
Start a standing weekly night that belongs only to sex: same candle, same playlist, calendar blocked. Tonight is the first one.
Sunrise picnic. Pack it the night before and bring a blanket big enough for everyone to hide under.
Museum date: each of you finds the piece that reminds you of the other. Big reveal over coffee after.
Thrift-store challenge: draw names, then $20 each to dress your person head to toe. Runway walk at the end.
Farmers market date: $15 each to build the best picnic you can. Then judge each other's haul.
Stargazing night: drive somewhere dark, lie back on a blanket, and name a constellation after each other.
Potluck where everyone brings the dish their family made when someone was sick. Tell the story before you serve.
Bookstore date: buy each other a book with a hidden note inside. No peeking until you're home.
Cook a dish from the country you most want to visit together. Set the table like you've already landed.
Slow dance in the kitchen to a song from the year you met. Burnt dinner is acceptable.
Plan a date for them using only clues. Send one riddle an hour until they work out where to show up.
Go back to the spot of your first date or first kiss. Order the same thing. Compare memories; whoever's wrong pays.
Game night: everyone teaches the group a game from their childhood. Winner picks the snacks for the next one.
Each of you secretly writes your pick: sunrise hike, fancy dinner, or a full day in pajamas. If you match, book it this week.
Rainy-day date: build a blanket fort and double-feature a movie from the year each of you was born.
Weekend away with no itinerary. Pick a direction, drive two hours, and say yes to whatever you find.
Secretly write your pick: a hotel night in your own city, a cabin with no signal, or one of you plans everything blind. Match? Book it.
Dinner where you can only ask each other questions you've never asked before. Repeat one and you're paying.
Go dancing somewhere loud, then walk home somewhere quiet. Hold hands the whole way.
Get dressed up for a date at home: separate rooms, a knock at the door, proper first-date nerves.
Give them a tour of you: the places that shaped you before you met. End at the one that matters most.
Recreate the night you first slept together, or the one you wish had happened. Same playlist, better lighting.
Late-night drive, no destination. Park somewhere with a view and climb into the back seat like you've got a curfew.
Each secretly circle one: a night of slow massages, a night trying something new, or a night one of you is in charge. Match? It's on this week.
Plan a whole-weekend date where every single stop is foreplay for the last one: the bedroom.
Blindfold them and feed them five tastes, one at a time. Every wrong guess earns a kiss.
An evening where nobody is allowed to rush: every kiss, touch, and sentence at half speed.
Kiss only their hands, wrists, and forearms for five slow minutes. Nowhere else, no matter how nicely they ask.
Share a candlelit bath. One rule: nobody mentions work, chores, or tomorrow.
Candlelit massage with warm oil. They choose where you start; you choose how long you stay.
Undress each other as slowly as possible: one minute per item, timer on, no skipping ahead.
Shower together where only one of you is allowed to do the washing. Switch tomorrow.
Trace an ice cube wherever they point. Then follow the trail with your mouth.
Map every spot that makes them shiver using only your fingertips. Report your findings out loud.
Loosely tie their wrists with a silk scarf and take your time everywhere. Untie the second they ask.
Spend an entire evening on foreplay. Set a one-hour timer before anyone's allowed to go further.
Have sex by candlelight with your eyes open the whole time. Say their name whenever you want to look away.
Blindfold yourself and let them guide your hands wherever they want to be touched, as slowly as they like.
Ask tonight, then tomorrow wake them up slowly, kissing your way down one inch at a time.
